cystic but with an irregular thick and enhancing wall, along

reports_summary.excerpt:
INDICATION:  post-op with intra-op femoral shaft fracture  // post-op with
intra-op femoral shaft fracture

COMPARISON:  Radiographs from ___

IMPRESSION: 

There is a right bipolar hemiarthroplasty. There is a long stem femoral
component with cerclage wires along the femoral shaft.  2 cortical screws are
seen within the distal femoral shaft fixating an oblique fracture of the
distal femoral shaft.  The fracture line is seen exiting the medial femoral
cortex distally.  No hardware related complications are seen.  No significant
changes seen from prior.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with malignant neoplasm of connective aand soft
tissue  // please place SL port.  pt to be admitted for chemo, please schedure
for AM thank you, ___

COMPARISON:  Chest CT ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ and Dr.
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure and has
reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
150 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 30 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS:  1 g ancef, 150 mcg fentanyl, 2 mg versed.
CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  0:29 min, 33 cGy.cm2

PROCEDURE
1. Right internal jugular approach chest single lumen Port-a-cath placement

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the explanation of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The upper chest was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent right internal jugular vein
was compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle. Permanent
ultrasound images were obtained before and after intravenous access, which
confirmed vein patency. Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the right
atrium using fluoroscopic guidance. The needle was exchanged for a
micropuncture sheath. The Nitinol wire was removed and a short ___ wire was
advanced to make appropriate measurements for catheter length. The ___ wire
was then passed distally into the IVC.
Next, attention was turned towards creation of a subcutaneous pocket over the
upper anterior chest wall. After instilling superficial and deeper local
anesthesia using lidocaine mixed with epinephrine, a 2.5 cm transverse
incision was made and a subcutaneous pocket was created by using blunt
dissection. The single lumen port was then connected to the catheter.  The
catheter was tunneled from the subcutaneous pocket towards the venotomy site
from where it was brought out using a tunneling device. The port was then
connected to the catheter and checks were made for any leakage by accessing
the diaphragm using a non-coring ___ needle. No leaks were found.
The port was then placed in the subcutaneous pocket and secured with ___
prolene sutures on either side. The venotomy tract was dilated using the
introducer of the peel-away sheath supplied. Following this, the peel-away
sheath was placed over the ___ wire through which the port was threaded into
the right side of the heart with the tip in the right atrium.  The sheath was
then peeled away.
The subcutaneous pocket was closed in layers with ___ interrupted and ___
subcuticular continuous Vicryl sutures.  Steri-strips were used to close the
venotomy incision site. Steri-Strips were applied over the sutures. Final spot
fluoroscopic image demonstrating good alignment of the catheter and no
kinking. The tip is in the right atrium.
The port was accessed using a non coring ___ needle and could be aspirated
and flushed easily. Sterile dressings were applied. The patient tolerated the
procedure well without immediate complication.  The port was left accessed as
requested.

FINDINGS: 

Patent right internal jugular vein. Final fluoroscopic image showing port with
catheter tip terminating in the right atrium.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a single lumen chest power Port-a-cath via the right
internal jugular venous approach. The tip of the catheter terminates in the
right atrium. The catheter is ready for use.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, Interventional Radiology Fellow and Dr.
___, attending radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
personally supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure
and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
50mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 20 during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine was injected
in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl, Versed
CONTRAST: 40 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  2 min, 13 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. IVC venogram.
2. Infrarenal Denali IVC filter deployment.
3. Post-filter placement venogram.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. the right neck was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
Under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance, the patent and compressible Right
internal jugular vein was punctured using a 21G micropuncture needle.
Ultrasound images of the access was stored on PACS. A ___ wire was
advanced through the micropuncture sheath into the inferior vena cava. A 8
___ sheath was exchanged for the micropuncture sheath and advanced into the
IVC. An inferior vena cava venogram was performed.

Based on the results of the venogram, detailed below, a decision was made to
place a infrarenal filter. The catheter and sheath were removed over the wire
and the sheath of an Denali filter was advanced over the wire into the IVC
past the take-off of the renal vessels. An inferior vena cava filter was
advanced over the wire until the cranial tip was at the level of the inferior
margin of the lower renal vein. The sheath was then withdrawn until the filter
was deployed. The wire and loading device were then removed through the sheath
and a repeat contrast injection was performed, confirming appropriate filter
positioning. The final image was stored on PACS.
The sheath was removed and pressure was held for 10 minutes,at which point
hemostasis was achieved. A sterile dressing was applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate post
procedure complications.

1. Patent normal sized, non-duplicated IVC with single bilateral renal veins
and no evidence of a clot.
2. Successful deployment of an infra-renal Denali IVC filter.

and enhancement throughout. Colon and rectum are within normal limits.  Though

appendicitis.  There is no evidence of mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  Again noted
is an enlarged right external iliac lymph node, it now measuring 5.4 x 3.4 cm,
previously 3.1 x 2.6 cm.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The visualized reproductive organs are unremarkable.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
The patient has undergone prior right total hip arthroplasty.

SOFT TISSUES: Again noted is a large hematoma along the right lateral body,
which extends to the mid/ distal femur.  Evaluation for active extravasation
is severely limited given significant metallic artifact from total right hip
arthroplasty.  No definite active extravasation is noted.  Approximate
dimension measure 10 x 8 x 30 cm.  Malignant involvement of this region is
difficult to assess, given metallic artifact and large hematoma.  .

IMPRESSION:


1. Extensive hematoma involving the right lateral thigh to at least the level
of the mid femur.  Within the limitations of the examination given beam
hardening artifact from the right hip prosthesis, no definite active bleeding
is identified.
2. Enlarging right external iliac lymph node.
3. New and enlarging pulmonary nodules.
4. Chronic right lower lobe pulmonary embolus.

thrombus.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:

2. Renal ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. The contour of the
liver is smooth. There is no focal liver mass. The main portal vein is patent
with hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 4 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 13.0 cm.

KIDNEYS: The right kidney measures 9.9 cm. The left kidney measures 10.5 cm.
Normal cortical echogenicity and corticomedullary differentiation is seen
bilaterally.  In the left upper pole renal cortex there is a 1.3 cm simple
renal cyst.  There is no evidence of concerning solid renal mass, stones, or
hydronephrosis in the kidneys.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

Unremarkable abdominal ultrasound.  Top normal spleen size (13.0 cm).  Patent
portal vein with normal direction of flow.  Note, ultrasound is not sensitive
for the detection of retroperitoneal hematoma.

of the right femur s/p radical resection in ___ s/p adjuvant

recently diagnosed recurrence in the pelvis and likely in the 
lungs with recurrent hemorrhage into the right leg 
sarcoma/hematoma and previous PE who presented with new 
incidental finding of PE on imaging. 

Pulmonary Embolism: 
- Patient with prior extensive bilateral PE diagnosed in ___ and IVC filter was placed in ___ given his ongoing 
hemorrhage into right thigh hematoma while on lovenox before 
ultimately stopping the lovenox due to persistent bleeding. 
Patient with incidental finding of large PE on follow-up 
imaging. He has been asymptomatic. He was briefly started on IV 
heparin but that was stopped. Troponins negative with mildly 
elevated BNP and no evidence of right heart strain on CT or EKG. 
He is high risk for bleeding while on anticoagulation due to 
ongoing uncontrolled bleeding and concern for compartment 
syndrome in the right lower extremity. Amputation was discussed 
to control ongoing bleeding at sarcoma site which would then 
allow for anticoagulation but this was determined to be a high 
risk in the setting of PEs and unclear benefit given decreased 
life expectancy and the decision was made by orthopedic surgery, 
the patient's primary oncologist and the patient to not proceed. 
The patient does have an IVC filter which placement was 
confirmed with imaging.

Acute Kidney Injury: 
- Likely pre-renal from decreased PO intake. Non-oliguric. 
Improved with IV Fluids.

Hypotension: 
- SBP ___. Patient asymptomatic. Likely due to hypovolemia. 
However on review baseline SPBs recently have been in the 100s. 
Improved with IV fluids.

Metastatic High-Grade Sarcoma of the Bone
- Now with local recurrence and distant mets to the lungs and 
brain. Lung mets had been relatively slow growing, although 
locoregional disease has been quite aggressive. He is s/p 
pallitative radiation to the thigh, although given persistent 
bleeding into hematoma and subsequent pain, he has been followed 
by orthopedics with consideration for radical amputation. No 
further chemotherapy treatment options. Palliative care and 
social work were consulted. A lengthy meeting was held with the 
orthopedic surgery, the patient's primary oncologist, the 
patient, and patient's family. It was decided that at this time 
the risks of an amputation would not outweigh the benefits. 
Given lack of further treatment options the patient has decided 
to transition to hospice care after underling cyberknife 
radiation to his brain metastasis next week. He does wish to 
continue receiving blood transfusions at this time as these 
improve  his quality of life. His current home care agency has a 
hospice agency but they are unable to allow blood transfusions 
so he will likely need to transition to a different hospice 
agency. His primary oncology office will assist with setting 
this up. A MOLST was filled out with the patient prior to 
discharge and he decided to be DNR/DNI.

Anemia/Thigh Hematoma: 
- Patient with known chronic hemorrhage into thigh 
sarcoma/hematoma. Has required significant transfusion support 
and currently receiving weekly blood transfusions at home. He is 
s/p 1 unit pRBCs on ___,  ___, and ___. Currently 
hemodynamically stable.

CNS Lesion: 
- MRI brain with solitary 12 x 8 mm right cerebellar enhancing 
lesion with thin rim of surrounding vasogenic edema concerning 
for metastasis. Currently no neurological symptoms. Discussed 
with Dr. ___ in Neuro ___, not recommending steroids or 
ant-epileptics at this time. He will follow-up with Radiation 
Oncology as an outpatient for stereotactic radiosurgery next 
week.

Cellulitis/Abscess: 
- Patient with chronic cyst on back that is currently 
erythematous, tender and draining purulent fluid. However, 
patient and family reports this has been present for many years 
and will intermittently express pus and never been incised or 
taken antibiotics. Ultrasound showed complex fluid collection. 
Continues to drain from sinus tract. No fevers or elevated WBC. 
Finished 7-day course of Bactrim and Keflex.

Thrombocytopenia: 
- Multifactorial. Currently stable.

Fever
- Isolated fever. No obvious source. Possibly due to disease. 
Blood and urine cultures negative at the time of discharge.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with IVC filter.  // Please evaluate IVC filter
position.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable supine abdominal radiograph

COMPARISON:  PET-CT dated ___

FINDINGS: 

There are no abnormally dilated loops of large or small bowel.
The IVC filter projects over the right side of the L2 and L3 vertebral bodies.
Osseous structures are unremarkable apart from a right hip hemiarthroplasty.
Mild degenerative changes of the lower lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION: 

The IVC filter projects over the right side of the L2 and L3 vertebral bodies.

EXAMINATION:  MR HEAD W AND W/O CONTRAST T9112 MR HEAD.

INDICATION:  History of metastatic sarcoma with PE and head CT demonstrating
small right cerebellar lesion.  Evaluate for metastatic disease.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal and axial T1 weighted imaging were performed. After
administration of 8 mL of Gadavist intravenous contrast, axial imaging was
performed with gradient echo, FLAIR, diffusion, and T1 technique. Sagittal
MPRAGE imaging was performed and re-formatted in axial and coronal
orientations.

COMPARISON:  Noncontrast head CT ___.

FINDINGS: 

Mildly hyperintense lesion in the right cerebellum corresponds to a 12 x 8 mm
enhancing lesion (900:69) with thin rim of surrounding vasogenic edema without
significant associated mass effect.  This lesion demonstrates slowed
diffusion.  There is no associated susceptibility artifact suggest hemorrhagic
transformation.  No additional enhancing lesion is identified.

There is no evidence of hemorrhage, significant mass effect, midline shift or
infarction.   The ventricles and sulci are normal in caliber and configuration
for age.  The principal intracranial vascular flow voids are preserved.  The
dural venous sinuses are patent on MP rage images.

The paranasal sinuses are grossly clear.  The orbits are grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

Solitary 12 x 8 mm right cerebellar enhancing lesion with thin rim of
surrounding vasogenic edema corresponding to CT findings, given history
compatible with metastasis.  No evidence of hemorrhagic transformation.  No
additional enhancing lesions.

EXAMINATION:  US, OTHER SOFT TISSUE AREA

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with draining abscess over back  // eval
drainable fluid collection

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale ultrasound images were obtained of the superficial
tissues of the left upper back.

COMPARISON:  None

FINDINGS: 

Transverse and sagittal images were obtained of the superficial tissues of the
left upper back.  In the area of clinical concern, there is a 2.6 x 3.1 x 0.9
cm predominantly hypoechoic fluid collection with peripheral hyperemia but no
central vascularity.  The collection demonstrates posterior acoustic
enhancement and low level internal echogenicity.  The superficial aspect of
the collection comes to the skin surface, and there is a suggestion draining
sinus tract.  The deep aspect of the collection is confined within the
superficial soft tissues.

IMPRESSION: 

2.6 x 3.1 x 0.9 cm complex fluid collection in the superficial tissues of the
left upper back with a draining sinus tract.   this would be amenable to
aspiration if clinically warranted.

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST Q111 CT HEAD.

INDICATION:  History: ___ with PE. CT head to r/o metastatic disease prior to
heparin  // ?mets.

contrast. Coronal and sagittal reformations as well as bone algorithm
reconstructions were provided and reviewed.

802.7 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Head) = 803 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

An 8 mm hyperdensity in the right cerebellum near midline with a small rim of
vasogenic edema is concerning for a focal mass, the possibility of small area
within this lesion associated with hemorrhagic transformation cannot be
completely rule out, correlation with MRI of the head with and without
contrast is recommended for further characterization.  The ventricles and
sulci prominent for the patient's age, suggesting cortical volume loss.

There is no evidence of fracture.  The visualized portion of the paranasal
sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are clear.  The visualized
portion of the orbits are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:


1. 8 mm hyperdensity in the right cerebellum with associated vasogenic edema
is concerning for a focal mass, possibly metastasis given the clinical
history.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Focal area of high attenuation identified in the right
cerebellum as described detail above, associated with vasogenic edema,
concerning for focal mass lesion, correlation with MRI of the head with and
without contrast recommended for further characterization.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with new lumbar sciatic symptoms,, history of
malignant sarcoma of the right proximal femur status post wide resection with
negative margins and reconstruction, status post chemotherapy.  Evaluate for
metastases to lumbar spine.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1 weighted, T2 weighted, and IDEAL images of the lumbar
spine with axial T1 and T2 weighted images. Following intravenous gadolinium
administration (8 cc Gadavist), sagittal and axial T1 weighted images were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  ___ FDG tumor imaging.

FINDINGS: 

There are 4 lumbar-type vertebrae and a partially sacralized L5.  Vertebral
body heights are within normal limits.  There is minimal retrolisthesis of L4
on L5.  Bone marrow signal is diffusely heterogenous on T1 and T2 weighted
images, without evidence for focal lesions on fat-suppressed IDEAL images. 
There are extensive discogenic bone marrow changes in the endplates from L2-L3
through L4-L5.

The distal spinal cord appears unremarkable, with the conus medullaris
terminating near the lower aspect of T12.  There is no abnormal intrathecal
contrast enhancement.

T12-L1:  Mild disc bulge and a small central/left paracentral disc protrusion.
No spinal canal narrowing and no significant neural foraminal narrowing.

L1-L2:  Mild bilateral facet arthropathy without spinal canal or neural
foraminal narrowing.

L2-L3:  Disc bulge and moderate facet arthropathy, as well as mild thickening
of the ligamentum flavum.  The subarticular zones are mildly narrowed without
compression of the traversing L3 nerve roots.  The thecal sac is slightly
narrowed without crowding of the intrathecal nerve roots.  There is mild to
moderate right neural foraminal narrowing with abutment of the exiting right
L2 nerve root by a facet osteophyte.  There is no significant left neural
foraminal narrowing.

L3-L4:  There is a disc bulge, larger on the left than right, as well as
thickening of the ligamentum flavum and moderate bilateral facet arthropathy. 
There is moderate spinal canal stenosis with crowding of the intrathecal nerve
roots, as well as abutment of bilateral traversing L4 nerve roots in the
subarticular zones with greater mass effect on the left than right.  There is
also mild to moderate right and mild left neural foraminal narrowing.

L4-L5:  There is a disc bulge, larger on the left than right, thickening of
the ligamentum flavum, and moderate, left greater than right facet
arthropathy.  There is left greater than right subarticular zone narrowing
with abutment of the traversing right L5 nerve root and displacement of the
traversing left L5 nerve root.  There is mild to moderate narrowing of the
thecal sac without significant crowding of the intrathecal nerve roots.  There
is mild to moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.

L5-S1:  The disc and facet joints are underdeveloped due to partial
sacralization of L5.  No spinal canal or neural foraminal narrowing.

1 cm left renal cyst on images 6:9, 9:9 appear simple.

IMPRESSION:


1. 4 lumbar-type vertebrae and a partially sacralized L5.
2. No evidence for an osseous or soft tissue mass in the lumbar spine.
3. Multilevel lumbar degenerative disease, as detailed above, including
moderate spinal canal narrowing at L3-L4, and mild spinal canal narrowing at
L2-L3 and L4-L5.
